bites.title: Recipes
bites.body: A modifier is a recipe Blender reruns every time anything changes. Edit the cube, and every copy, bevel, and wobble updates with it.

bites.title: Array
bites.body: Properties, wrench tab, Add Modifier, Generate, Array. Two cubes in a row.
bites.hint: The wrench tab in the Properties editor. Add Modifier is the big button.

bites.title: Mind the gap
bites.body: Under Relative Offset, set Factor X to 1.5. Now there's space between them.
bites.hint: Expand Relative Offset if it's folded. Factor X is the first field.

bites.title: Into a grid
bites.body: Add a second Array. In its Relative Offset, set Factor X to 0 and Factor Y to 1.5. A train becomes a parking lot.
bites.hint: A second Array modifier goes below the first. X to 0, Y to 1.5.

bites.title: Jungle gym
bites.body: Add Modifier, Generate, Wireframe. Every edge turns into a beam.

bites.title: Change the source
bites.body: Scale the cube with S. Watch the whole grid update. That's the power: one edit, everything follows.

bites.title: Remove one
bites.body: Delete the Wireframe modifier: hover its panel and press Ctrl+X, or use its dropdown and pick Delete.

bites.title: Make it real
bites.body: Hover the first Array and press Ctrl+A to apply it (or dropdown, Apply). The recipe gets cooked into real geometry, for better or worse.
bites.hint: Apply the top Array. The mesh jumps from 8 vertices to 40.

bites.title: Lesson 07: cleared
bites.body:
Array, Wireframe, stacking, live updates, deleting, applying. Non-destructive is a mindset: keep the recipe as long as you can.

Scroll on for Lesson 08: color and shine.
